# Repo Facts

Repository text encoding default: UTF-8 without BOM.
Files containing Chinese must be saved as UTF-8 without BOM. Do not convert project text files to ANSI, Big5, UTF-8 BOM, or other locale-dependent encodings.
MSVC source compilation in this repo is configured for UTF-8 via `/utf-8` in `CMakeLists.txt`, and edited repository text files should stay UTF-8 without BOM.
Win32 UI boundaries may still require wide strings / UTF-16 helpers, but repository text files and exchanged text payloads should stay UTF-8 without BOM.

- 2026-05-08 verified-by-source: the Windows near-RT EtherCAT baseline now includes a dedicated cyclic thread, process/thread priority and affinity tuning, CPU isolation monitoring, receive-before-send non-blocking PDO polling (`ecx_receive_processdata(..., 0)`), bounded DC PI drift compensation, QPC plus high-resolution wait timing with invariant-TSC fine spin for the short tail, VirtualLock/working-set tuning, background status-log writing, lock-free UI cache reads, NIC RSS affinity help, and adapter warm-up; the main remaining gaps versus `docs/soem_windows_500us.md` are ETW/interrupt-latency analysis, NIC advanced-property auditing beyond RSS, and explicit cache-alignment, prefetch, or NUMA-aware optimization.
- 2026-05-08 verified-by-source: connect-time NIC optimization now includes a best-effort wireless IRQ rebalance step that targets active WiFi and Bluetooth PAN adapters for RSS rebalancing onto non-RT cores below the protected Core 4 range, and also audits Bluetooth PnP devices for a standard interrupt-affinity policy path without auto-writing registry overrides; failures remain non-fatal and are logged because many wireless drivers do not expose RSS controls or require elevation.

- 2026-05-10 verified: simulation `AdvanceSimulation()` must mirror real EtherCAT PDO timing by updating virtual feedback from the IOmap command already sent in the prior cycle, then applying `stagedOutputs` for the next cycle. Applying staged filter outputs before virtual plant integration creates zero-cycle feedback and makes Auto Connect/PDOFilter soft-start differ from field behavior.

During healthy CSV soft-start the filter may hold issued output near the tightened 5-degree tracking window while the axis catches up; abort only when the filter reports `IsError()` or `IsTrackingErrorFatal()`.
- 2026-05-09 verified: PDOFilter/UI display can normalize `0x6064`/`0x607A` positions to a single turn, but CSV control must unwrap actual position near the current filter command/reference before passing feedback into `PDOFilter::Filter()`. Otherwise crossing +/-180 degrees in simulation or field feedback looks like a 360-degree tracking jump, destabilizing `0x60FF` velocity and latching false tracking errors.
- 2026-05-10 verified: `PDOFilter::Filter()` final-output ordering must apply the `iActValue ± trackingErrorWindow` clamp first and then a hard `[iMinPDO_, iMaxPDO_]` clamp last; otherwise when `iActValue` is already past a configured PDO position limit (manual push, tightened limits mid-flight, or a fault) the tracking-error window expands the output back outside the PDO envelope and the slave is told to move further past the limit. When the hard PDO clamp engages and `oCurrentVelocity_` still points outward, bleed it toward zero using at least the configured deceleration (`max(abs(iMaxDeceleration_), abs(iConfiguredMaxDeceleration_)) * iCycleTime_`) so CSV `feedforwardVelocity = GetInternalVelocity()` does not retain a residual outward velocity that keeps `0x60FF` driving the motor at constant speed past the limit. Guarded by `tests/test_pdofilter_pdo_limit_velocity_decay.cpp` (closed-loop and stuck-actual-past-limit cases for both upper and lower PDO limits).
- 2026-05-10 verified: `PDOFilter::Filter()` `MeasurementMismatch` handling must clamp the original incoming command into `iActValue ± trackingErrorWindow`; do not replace it with the stale issued-command side (`iActValue + copysign(window, issuedCommand-actual)`) and do not source it from a prior input-anomaly prediction. Otherwise after the user/MMF input returns low, tracking-error protection can keep commanding the old outward boundary and make Filter output run away while the Filter input trace stays low. When tracking/hard-limit safety boundaries are active, braking/bleed must use configured decel even if global limiting has reduced current decel to the soft-start ratio; the field signature was `A=-120` after a 600 deg/s² config, which leaves enough stopping distance for a 70-90 deg/s residual velocity to hit the position limit. In addition, `EtherCATMaster::ComputeCsvVelocityCommand()` must inhibit CSV correction directionally with `PDOFilter::GetTrackingClampDirection()` and immediately clear same-direction outward `correctionVelocity`/`commandVelocity` components; otherwise a stale positive `0x60FF` target can continue pushing the virtual/real axis after the filter boundary engages. Guarded by the tracking guard-source, configured-decel safety-braking, tracking-window-bleed, and tracking-error-recovery blocks in `tests/test_pdofilter_velocity_continuity.cpp`; validated with focused PDOFilter CTest (4/4) and Release smoke (20/20).
- 2026-05-09 verified: CSV `0x60FF` must be a closed-loop velocity command derived from filter feedforward plus `(filtered target - actual position)` correction under the current PDOFilter velocity/deceleration limits; using only the filter output derivative can leave actual feedback stopped away from target, so Pose6D virtual Auto Connect soft-start never becomes ready. Guarded by `tests/test_simulation_pose6d_softstart_completes.cpp` plus the CSV soft-start smoke tests.
- 2026-05-09 verified: Auto Connect completion must preserve AutoWindow `oOnline` when PDO filtering remains enabled; the completion path should clear only the busy bit and derive the online bit from `EtherCATMaster::IsPDOFilteringEnabled()`. Sending owner state `0` after a successful CSV soft-start can briefly or permanently extinguish the online lamp even though cyclic filtering is active.
- 2026-05-09 verified: simulation/online Filter velocity telemetry should publish PDOFilter internal planned velocity/acceleration, because final-output delta velocity is disturbed by tracking-window clamps and appears unstable in RT scope. CSV feedforward may use that internal velocity after soft-start, but soft-start `0x60FF` must stay capped to the soft-start velocity envelope plus the bounded CSV correction margin so Pose6D soft-start still completes without exceeding the existing velocity guard. Guarded by `tests/test_simulation_filter_velocity_stability.cpp`, `tests/test_simulation_pose6d_softstart_completes.cpp`, and Smoke Test (16/16 passed).
- 2026-05-09 verified: simulation Filter-speed sawtooth was caused by PDOFilter input-anomaly replacement during sparse MMF updates. After several stale/predicted cycles, the replacement must continue from `ioPrevEffectiveSetpoint_`; anchoring back to the previous raw MMF sample creates a real backward snap in the effective target and a visible velocity kink. Continuous per-cycle jumps should still use the raw-sample anchor so tracking-mismatch protection reports `MeasurementMismatch`. Guarded by tightened `tests/test_simulation_filter_velocity_stability.cpp` (`maxVelocityJump <= 3.0`), `tests/test_pdofilter_velocity_continuity.cpp`, and Smoke Test (16/16 passed).
- 2026-05-09 verified: simulation-mode PDOFilter must use MMFReader per-axis update counters, not value equality alone, to distinguish real new MMF samples from held samples. In simulation, `FilterWithInputState(..., allowPrediction=false)` consumes the actual MMF-held value without prediction substitution; Pose6D input treats any source pose-channel update as a new sample for all six derived servo-angle setpoints. Guarded by `tests/test_pdofilter_velocity_continuity.cpp`, `tests/test_simulation_filter_velocity_stability.cpp`, and Smoke Test (16/16 passed).
- 2026-05-09 verified: PDOFilter's prediction-return bridge (`(raw + movingAverage) / 2`) must only run after the previous cycle actually used prediction. When simulation consumes real held MMF samples with prediction disabled, applying that bridge on the first new sample makes the effective setpoint jump forward then fall back to the moving average on the next held cycle, producing real Filter-output instability. Guarded by the held-MMF step regression in `tests/test_pdofilter_velocity_continuity.cpp` and the 1ms-sampled `tests/test_simulation_filter_velocity_stability.cpp`; Smoke Test passed 16/16.
- 2026-05-09 verified: RT scope/MMF fields `tPos`, `tVel`, `aPos`, and `aVel` must stay sourced from the PDO snapshot reads for `0x607A`, `0x60FF`, `0x6064`, and `0x606C` respectively. Do not overwrite those fields with predicted MMF/filter-internal values; `filter`, `filterVel`, and `filterAcc` are the dedicated PDOFilter telemetry channels. Validated with `build_incremental-Crash.ps1 -NonInteractive`, focused CSV/filter CTest, and Smoke Test (16/16 passed).

- 2026-05-10 verified: PDOFilter global limiting must distinguish "limiting still forced by the master" from "this slave still has an active violation". - 2026-05-10 verified: `EtherCATMaster::UpdateGlobalViolationState()` should keep the global violation latch debounced, but it must release per-axis physical global limiting (`SetGlobalLimitingEnabled(false)`) as soon as no active violation remains. - 2026-05-10 verified: PDOFilter dynamic velocity/accel violations must keep axes moving by capping `iMaxVelocity_` at the configured velocity-violation threshold, not at the soft-start crawl ratio (`SOFT_START_VEL_RATIO`). - 2026-05-10 verified: when MMF input oscillates with large amplitude but stays within [iMinPDO_, iMaxPDO_], `PDOFilter::Filter()` keeps output strictly within the configured PDO envelope and does not exhibit growing-amplitude resonance. This invariant is now guarded across centred sine, off-centre sine that approaches the upper/lower PDO limit, and square-wave drives at multiple frequencies/servo lags by `tests/test_pdofilter_oscillating_input_within_limits.cpp`. The protection comes from two independent clamps in `Filter()`: the `effectiveSetpoint = clamp(target, iActValue - trackingErrorWindow, iActValue + trackingErrorWindow)` window plus the unconditional final `clamp(finalResult, iMinPDO_, iMaxPDO_)` (with the safety velocity bleed when the hard clamp engages); both must be preserved together to keep this contract.
- 2026-05-11 verified: `PDOFilter::Filter()` must rate-limit the tracking-error-window clamp result after the `iActValue +/- trackingErrorWindow` window is applied. The per-cycle step from `ioPrevFilteredOutput_` must stay within `max(abs(iConfiguredMaxVelocity_), abs(iMaxVelocity_)) * iCycleTime_`; otherwise the `GetFilteredOutput()` trace can jump by tens of degrees in one cycle and push `iActValue` past the hard PDO limit, triggering `AutoEmergencyStop`. Keep this rate limit between the tracking window clamp and the final hard `[iMinPDO_, iMaxPDO_]` clamp, skip it when `trackingErrorFatalTriggered` snaps output back to `iActValue`, and do not resync `oCurrentVelocity_`. Guarded by `tests/test_pdofilter_velocity_continuity.cpp` and `tests/test_pdofilter_pdo_limit_velocity_decay.cpp`; validated with focused PDOFilter CTest and full Release Smoke Test.
- 2026-05-11 verified (supersedes earlier same-day note): `PDOFilter::Filter()` final-output ordering is: (1) tracking-error window clamp, (2) hard PDO clamp with velocity bleed so `GetInternalVelocity()` stops feeding outward motion past the limit, (3) final acceleration limit on the committed position step, and (4) fatal-tracking recovery handling. The planning loop velocity ramp remains the source of inter-cycle continuity; the hard-limit bleed handles outward-velocity decay, and the acceleration limit only bounds per-cycle position movement. `tests/test_pdofilter_velocity_continuity.cpp` therefore checks gradual convergence rather than an instant one-cycle snap.
- 2026-05-11 verified (supersedes earlier 2026-05-11 entries): on non-fatal cycles, the final acceleration envelope remains the single source of truth for how far `finalResult` may move in one cycle. On fatal-tracking cycles, the safety target still clamps toward `iActValue` and the implementation then zeros velocity and acceleration so later cycles ramp from rest without injecting an RT-scope position jump. Guarded by `tests/test_pdofilter_velocity_continuity.cpp`, `tests/test_pdofilter_pdo_limit_velocity_decay.cpp`, `tests/test_simulation_softstart_no_fatal_tracking`, and `tests/test_simulation_multiturn_actual_position_normalized`; validated with focused PDOFilter CTest and Release Smoke Test.
- 2026-05-11 simulation virtual-mode actual-position teleports: `src/ethercat/EtherCATMaster.Simulation.cpp` contains explicit `axis.actualPositionCounts = target` teleports in three places: (a) homing completion when `closeEnough || maxActiveElapsed`, (b) CSV settle short-circuit when `targetDelta`, `targetVelocity`, `actualVelocity`, and `positionError` are all within the settle thresholds for `kSimulationCsvSettleStableSec`, and (c) the residual settle path in `stepPositionLoop` when the remaining error is negligible. The homing and CSV settle teleports are deliberate convergence shortcuts, but they also appear as `iActValue` discontinuities to `PDOFilter` and as visible RT-scope jumps in virtual mode. They do not occur on real EtherCAT slaves. Decision pending from user before changing or removing these teleports.
- 2026-05-12 verified (supersedes 2026-05-11 PDOFilter ordering notes): `PDOFilter::Filter()` delegates to `FilterWithInputState()`, and `FilterWithInputState()` is the implementation owner for CSV-safe filtering. - 2026-05-17 verified: when actual feedback oscillates outside the PDOFilter tracking window while the upstream MMF/input command is held or moving the opposite way, actual-driven tracking-window clamp motion must not be republished as `PDOFilter::GetInternalVelocity()` / CSV feedforward. `Filter輸出` may still move under the safety clamp, but `Filter速度` must stay tied to commanded motion intent or bleed toward zero so 0x60FF does not amplify feedback lag. - 2026-05-17 verified: soft-start CSV feedforward consumes `PDOFilter::GetCurrentVelocity()` (published output velocity), not `GetInternalVelocity()`. - 2026-05-17 verified (partly superseded by 2026-05-22 CSV tuning): physical CSV position-error correction in `EtherCATMaster::ComputeCsvVelocityCommand()` must not remain a pure high-gain `Kp * (filteredOutput - actualPosition)` loop, and position P gain must remain auxiliary rather than the primary drive. Separate soft-start final pull-in from post-soft-start hold: while soft-start is active and feedforward has settled near zero, allow a bounded pull-in correction so axes can enter the ready window; after soft-start completion, use the smaller hold correction gain/velocity cap so a held target does not oscillate. - 2026-05-17 verified: after normal soft-start, a physical MMF over-acceleration input must not leave `PDOFilter` stuck on the old predicted trajectory. While dynamic limiting/detection suspension is active, in-range `ExceededAccelLimit` guard replacements should advance by a bounded step toward the new MMF input instead of repeatedly substituting the old prediction; if the MMF raw sample has already reversed toward the filter effective setpoint, recovery must follow that raw-delta direction instead of chasing the old far endpoint. PDO-limit jumps and measurement-mismatch guards remain safety clamps. When an axis has its own dynamic velocity/acceleration/deceleration violation, restore both configured acceleration (P4) and deceleration (P5), because braking an old negative-direction motion requires positive acceleration; if an axis is only globally force-limited, keep the softer global envelope until it has its own dynamic violation. Guarded by measured-velocity recovery/global-accel-decel regressions in `tests/test_pdofilter_velocity_continuity.cpp`; validated with Release incremental build, focused PDOFilter/soft-start simulation executables, and Release Smoke 24/24.
- 2026-05-17 verified: CSV tracking-window safety inhibition in `EtherCATMaster::ComputeCsvVelocityCommand()` must distinguish actual-driven sliding-window outward motion from commanded tracking recovery. - 2026-05-17 verified: during PDOFilter soft-start, velocity planning must still cap desired velocity by stopping distance to the current raw command target (clamped to active PDO limits), even when the tracking-window effective setpoint is moving with feedback. - 2026-05-21 verified: after PDOFilter soft-start completes, normal online motion uses a 2-degree protected edge inside configured PDO limits when the limit span is wide enough. - 2026-05-21 verified (superseded by 2026-05-22 moving-feedforward refinement): CSV `ComputeCsvVelocityCommand()` must clear same-direction correction when actual feedback leads the filtered command target; same-direction feedforward/command velocity is bled or cleared only in low-speed/hold lead-inhibit and hard/protected-edge safety states. Snapping command velocity causes visible post-soft-start 0x60FF jumps, but hard-zeroing moving feedforward can turn a smooth `Filter速度` into intermittent `0x60FF` pulses when feedback phase/noise briefly leads the command. CSV hard-limit logic must use the same 2-degree post-soft-start protected motion limits as PDOFilter and immediately refresh IOmap 0x60FF when the protected edge is reached. PDOFilter lead-suppressed tracking clamps must use the raw incoming command, not the actual-window-adjusted effective setpoint, when deciding whether committed motion matches operator command intent; this preserves faulted lower-limit convergence without allowing sliding actual feedback to drag the filter toward the limit. Guarded by `tests/test_pdofilter_velocity_continuity.cpp`, `tests/test_pdofilter_violation_no_runaway.cpp`, `tests/test_simulation_filter_velocity_stability.cpp`, and `tests/test_simulation_csv_hard_limit_no_outward_velocity.cpp`; validated with focused tests and Release Smoke 25/25.
